title: Evidence-sidecar verification accepts refs with empty or malformed sha256 values

finding.claim: Evidence-sidecar verification accepts refs with empty or malformed sha256 values
finding.recommendation: Reject refs whose sha256 is not exactly 64 lowercase hex characters before attempting to load a sidecar file, and report them as invalid evidence refs. This should mirror the strict hash-format checks used elsewhere in the file.

refutation.reason: No panel refutation was recorded for this finding — it reached the workup undisputed. The opposing/confirmatory position is the executed probe in SS3 of the packet: Sidecar-sha probe (`probes/closingA_sidecar_sha.py`) drives `core._validate_evidence_sidecars` directly (function at core.py:5855; cited line at core.py:5873 at HEAD) with hand-made refs. Every malformed shape fails closed — the problems list is non-empty in all four cases: - empty sha (`''`) → `sidecar file missing` - non-hex sha (`'zz-not-a-hash'`) → `sidecar file missing` - well-formed but absent sha (`'a'×64`) → `sidecar file missing` - traversal sha (`'../outside.txt'`) naming a REAL file outside the evidence dir → the file is loaded, then rejected: `sidecar content does not hash to its ref (tampered or corrupt)` - control (a genuine ref produced by `_attach_evidence_sidecars`) → problems=[] — valid refs still validate The mechanism is structural: the digest is used simultaneously as the sidecar's filename inside the evidence dir and as the expected hash of its content, so a ref validates only if a file exists whose own sha256 equals the ref string. No malformed value can satisfy that. Re-run at HEAD `61e137d` produced byte-identical output (sha256 unchanged, §5).
refutation.provenance: none-recorded: no dispute exists in the source record; the workup probe is the only counter-position
